scope: From Mithlond's front page: "Data centers are coming to Hampton Roads. The question is who will own them, who will pay the costs, and who will share in any benefit." Its three questions: "Who Can Own This?" ("Can a municipality, port authority, or utility district own and operate compute infrastructure? What would that cost? What legal structures exist in Virginia?"), "Who Bears the Cost?" ("Data centers consume water and electricity at enormous scale. In a region already facing accelerating flood risk, who absorbs those externalities — and who decides?") and "Who Gets the Benefit?" ("If the infrastructure lands here, does Norfolk's workforce, its universities, its communities get a structural piece — or just construction jobs?"). In scope: data centers and compute in Hampton Roads (Norfolk, Virginia Beach, Chesapeake, Portsmouth, Suffolk, Hampton, Newport News, Isle of Wight and neighbors); Virginia law, tax policy, utility rates and grid capacity that govern them; their water, power and flood exposure; public or community ownership of compute anywhere, as a model.
open_questions: Track D2: any new data center permit applications in Hampton Roads filed since January 2026 (research/TASKS.md).
Track D1: current operators and announced expansions at 3800 Village Ave and Corporate Landing (Virginia Beach).
Track C4: statutory provisions that let a public authority (e.g. BVU Authority) run broadband or utility service.
Track E2: Hampton Roads delegation members on the General Assembly's Finance and Commerce and Labor committees.
Dominion's rates and rate classes for large loads (the GS-5 class above 25 MW) and the interconnection queue.
Virginia's data center retail sales and use tax exemption (DCRSUT): repeal, extension or conditions.
The Southside Network Authority's regional fiber ring: completion and open-access terms.
